target: Karate yapan sporcu dizini sakatladı.
english: The athlete who does karate injured his knee.
tip: -an makes a who does relative. Karate yapan sporcu means the athlete who does karate, with no separate who word.

target: Kanka, akşam buluşalım mı?
english: Buddy, shall we meet tonight?
tip: The -alım ending makes a we-suggestion: buluşalım = let's meet. Adding mı turns it into a question, so buluşalım mı asks shall we.

target: Okuduğum kitap çok heyecanlıydı.
english: The book I read was very exciting.
tip: Okuduğum means that I read: the -dığım ending on a verb builds a relative clause, so Okuduğum kitap = the book that I read.

target: Denizin sesini dinleyerek uykuya dalmak harika.
english: It's wonderful falling asleep listening to the sound of the sea.
tip: The -erek ending means by doing something: dinleyerek = by listening, telling you how the falling asleep happens.

target: Otobüs geç geldiği için toplantıya yetişemedim.
english: I couldn't make it to the meeting because the bus was late.
tip: geldiği için means because it came: a verb plus -dığı için gives the reason, here why I missed the meeting.

target: Pazar günleri genellikle geç kalkıp kahvaltı hazırlarız.
english: On Sundays we usually wake up late and prepare breakfast.
tip: kalkıp uses -ıp to chain verbs under one tense: geç kalkıp kahvaltı hazırlarız = we wake up late and make breakfast.

target: Onunla konuştukça fikirlerinin ne kadar farklı olduğunu anlıyorum.
english: The more I talk with him/her, the more I understand how different their ideas are.
tip: konuştukça uses -dıkça for the more, the more: konuştukça anlıyorum = the more I talk, the more I understand.

target: Geçen yaz tatile gitmek yerine evde kalıp bahçeyle uğraştık.
english: Last summer instead of going on vacation we stayed home and worked on the garden.
tip: gitmek yerine means instead of going: an infinitive plus yerine expresses choosing one action over another.

target: Mektuplar her sabah sekizde dağıtılır.
english: Letters are distributed at eight every morning.
tip: dağıtılır is passive: the -ıl ending drops the doer, so it means letters are distributed with no mention of who does it.

target: Kış geceleri ailece tombala oynardık.
english: On winter nights we used to play bingo as a family.
tip: oynardık means we used to play: the -rdık ending marks a repeated past habit, not a single event.

target: Ne yaparsam yapayım onu memnun edemiyorum.
english: Whatever I do I can't please him.
tip: Ne yaparsam yapayım means whatever I do: the frame repeats the verb, yaparsam then yapayım, to say no matter what.

target: İstanbul'a her gidişimde yeni bir yer keşfediyorum.
english: Every time I go to Istanbul I discover a new place.
tip: her gidişimde means every time I go: her plus the verbal noun gidiş with -imde marks each occasion something happens.

target: Fatma'nın araştırma makalesi konunun bütüncül bir analizini sunuyor.
english: Fatma's research article presents a comprehensive analysis of the topic.
tip: Turkish adds an apostrophe before a suffix on a proper name: Fatma'nın = Fatma's, keeping the name readable.

target: Her ne kadar yorgun olsam da işimi bitirmeliyim.
english: No matter how tired I am I must finish my work.
tip: Her ne kadar with a later da means although: Her ne kadar yorgun olsam da = no matter how tired I am.

target: Her yıl sonbahar gelince yapraklar dökülür.
english: Every year when autumn comes the leaves fall.
tip: The -ince ending means when or as soon as: gelince = when it comes, so sonbahar gelince is when autumn arrives.

target: Çocuklar bahçede top oynayarak vakit geçirdi.
english: The children spent time playing ball in the garden.
tip: The -arak ending means by doing something: oynayarak = by playing, showing how they spent the time.

target: O kararı vermeseydi hayatı çok farklı olurdu.
english: If he had not made that decision, his life would be very different.
tip: vermeseydi (if he had not made it) sets up an unreal past, and olurdu (would be) gives the imagined result.

target: Her ne kadar yorgun olsam da işimi bitirmem gerekiyor.
english: Although I am very tired I need to finish my work.
tip: Her ne kadar opens a concession closed by -sa da: olsam da = even though I am, so it reads although I am tired.

target: Bu saate kadar eve varmış olmalılar.
english: They should have arrived home by this time.
tip: varmış olmalılar joins past -mış with olmalı (must) to infer about the past: they must have arrived by now.

target: Nazar değmesin diye mavi boncuk takarız.
english: We wear blue beads to ward off the evil eye.
tip: diye after a verb marks purpose: değmesin diye = so that it does not touch, here to keep the evil eye away.

target: Köyde elektrik kesilince mum ışığında otururduk.
english: When the power went out in the village we used to sit by candlelight.
tip: The -urduk ending is past habitual: otururduk = we used to sit, a repeated past routine, not one single sitting.

target: Sınav sonuçları gelince çok sevineceğim.
english: I will be very happy when the exam results come.
tip: gelince means when it comes. The -ince ending marks the moment one action triggers another, so no separate word for when is needed.

target: İzlediğimiz film ödül kazanmış.
english: The movie we watched apparently won an award.
tip: kazanmış uses the -mış past for things you did not witness yourself, giving a sense of apparently or so I heard rather than a plain fact.

target: Gördüğüm en güzel manzara burasıydı.
english: This was the most beautiful view I've seen.
tip: Gördüğüm means that I saw and describes manzara. The -dığım ending turns a verb into a relative clause modifying the following noun.

target: Babam emekli olduktan sonra bahçeyle uğraşmaya başladı.
english: My dad started gardening after he retired.
tip: olduktan sonra means after becoming. The -dıktan sonra pattern on a verb marks doing the main action after that one finishes.

target: Sen eve gelene kadar ben temizliği bitirmiş olurum.
english: By the time you come home I'll have finished the cleaning.
tip: gelene kadar means until you come. The -ene kadar ending sets a deadline that the main action reaches or finishes by.

target: Bir uzmana danışsaydın daha iyi olurdu.
english: It would have been better if you had consulted a specialist.
tip: danışsaydın is the if you had consulted form. The -saydın ending marks a past condition that did not actually happen.

target: Nerelisiniz?
english: Where are you from?
tip: -li turns a place into from there: nere plus -li plus -siniz gives Nerelisiniz, where are you from.

target: Yirmi beş yaşındayım.
english: I'm twenty-five years old.
tip: yaşındayım = I am ... years old: yaş (age) + -ında + -yım. Turkish states age with this being ending, no verb for to be.

target: Bu yer boş mu?
english: Is this seat free?
tip: The yes/no word harmonizes with the last vowel: after boş (o) it becomes mu, so Bu yer boş mu asks is this seat free.
